speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The government introduced three repeal bills to remove over 900 redundant Commonwealth acts, including the Wool International Act 1993, the Wool International Privatisation Act 1999, and the Papua and New Guinea Loan (International Bank) Act 1970, and to abolish the Medical Training Review Panel and the Fishing Industry Policy Council, while simplifying aged-care provider notifications to save $1.16 million annually in compliance costs.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The Statute Law Revision Bill (No. 3) 2015 was moved to repeal spent or redundant legislation and correct minor errors in Commonwealth laws, including amending the Child Support (Registration and Collection) Act 1988 to bind the Crown in right of the Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory, modernising offence provisions, updating indexation terms, and removing obsolete provisions such as the review requirement under the Do Not Call Register Act 2006.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the government's red tape repeal bills are largely symbolic, with only $6.9 million in claimed savings—1.4% of the $4.5 billion total—and that over half the measures are recycled from a previous bill. The speaker also announced Labor would reinstate the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines and criticised a measure reducing penalties for employers who fail to pay superannuation on time.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speech supported the Omnibus Repeal Day (Spring 2015), Amending Acts 1990-1999 Repeal, and Statute Law Revision (No. 3) bills as deregulation measures, opposing Labor's ETS as a cost-of-living increase and citing $1 billion in monthly interest on previous government debt. It argued overregulation had forced remittance businesses underground and that the Moorebank rail freight project would increase particulate matter nine-fold.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The three repeal day bills repeal over 900 Commonwealth acts, with the government reporting $2 billion in red tape reductions and a $4.5 billion annual decrease in compliance costs since September 2013.
